scenarios.title: The Kicking Records Board
scenarios.text: Your name goes up on the club's kicking records board.

choices.label: Bring {holder}
choices.result: You bring {holder} to see it. Their name should be there too.

choices.label: Aim for more
choices.result: You look at the next name on the list.

choices.label: Take a picture
choices.result: You take a picture for {parent}.

scenarios.title: The Team's Anniversary
scenarios.text: The club celebrates its fiftieth anniversary with a gala, a banner of club legends across the stadium, and your face is on it, between two Hall of Famers.

choices.label: Meet the old players
choices.result: Players from every era of the club, met one by one at the gala. One of them held for your childhood hero, and he tells you everything.

choices.label: Speak at the event
choices.result: A short speech, on stage, about what the club has meant to you. The old players clap the loudest, and one of them cries.

choices.label: Enjoy it with your family
choices.result: Your family, in the stands, under the banner, quietly. {parent} takes forty photos of your face on the banner, all slightly blurry.

scenarios.title: The Veteran's Union Meeting
scenarios.text: The veterans meet about the next labor agreement in a hotel conference room, and it's tense: pensions, health care, the length of the season. Somebody throws a chair.

choices.label: Speak for the specialists
choices.result: The specialists, spoken for, because nobody else was going to. The union adds two lines about kickers to the proposal.

choices.label: Read every clause
choices.result: Every clause of the proposal, read overnight. You find the one about injury guarantees that matters most, and you flag it.

choices.label: Vote with the room
choices.result: Your vote goes with the room, and your opinions stay for the bus. The meeting ends, and nobody throws anything else.

scenarios.title: The Teammate in Rehab
scenarios.text: A teammate goes into a long rehab for a knee injury that may end his career. He's thirty-four and has three kids, and he stops answering texts after the second surgery.

choices.label: Visit him every week
choices.result: Every week, at his house, whether he wants it or not. Some weeks you just watch television together, and some weeks he talks.

choices.label: Keep his locker as it was
choices.result: His locker, kept exactly as it was, with his name on it, at your insistence. The room remembers him every day.

choices.label: Send a message
choices.result: A warm, short message every few weeks. He replies with a thumbs-up months later, and you're glad you kept sending them.

scenarios.title: The Kicking Camp Partner
scenarios.text: A college coach asks you to co-host a kicking camp in July: two hundred high school kickers, three days, a university field and your name on the poster.

choices.label: Co-host it
choices.result: Three days, co-hosted, from dawn to dusk. It's a great week, and five of the kids end up with college scholarships.

choices.label: Bring {holder} along
choices.result: {holder}, recruited to run the holding station. The campers love the two of you together, and {holder} is better with teenagers than you.

choices.label: Pass this year
choices.result: Not this year, you tell the coach. He says the offer stands, and you spend July at the lake with your family.

scenarios.title: Baby Number Two
scenarios.text: A second child, and the house feels half its size. Everyone is tired, nobody is sleeping, and the season starts in three weeks.

choices.label: Take the night shift
choices.result: You take the night shifts on your off days. You're exhausted at practice and closer to {love_interest} than you've been in years.

choices.label: Make a plan
choices.result: You make a plan for the season, down to who sleeps when. It works about half the time, which is better than nothing.

choices.label: Ask the grandparents
choices.result: You ask the grandparents to come for a month. Everyone sleeps, and the house is loud and full in the best way.

scenarios.title: The School Play
scenarios.text: Your kid's school play is the night before a road game.

choices.label: Go to the play
choices.result: You go to the play and catch a late flight.

choices.label: Watch the dress rehearsal
choices.result: You watch the dress rehearsal instead.

choices.label: Watch the video
choices.result: You watch the video on the plane, twice. Your kid forgives you faster than you forgive yourself.

scenarios.title: The Parent-Teacher Conference
scenarios.text: You go to your first parent-teacher conference and get recognized by the teacher.

choices.label: Laugh about it
choices.result: You laugh about it and focus on your kid.

choices.label: Ask good questions
choices.result: You ask good questions. The teacher forgets you kick.

choices.label: Keep it short
choices.result: You keep it short and leave with a list of spelling words.

scenarios.title: The Family Dog
scenarios.text: The family dog is getting old, and the kids are asking questions.

choices.label: Answer honestly
choices.result: You answer honestly. It's a hard and good talk.

choices.label: Find a good book
choices.result: You find a good book about it and read it together.

choices.label: Spend the time
choices.result: You spend more time with the dog. The kids join you on the slow walks.

scenarios.title: The Partner's New Job
scenarios.text: {love_interest} gets a big job offer of their own, in a city you'd never live in during the season. They're excited, and trying not to show it.

choices.label: Back them all the way
choices.result: You back them all the way and work out the travel later. Your life gets busier and lonelier, and {love_interest} glows every time you call.

choices.label: Make it work together
choices.result: You sit down with a calendar and make a plan that works for both careers. It's complicated and fair, and it holds.

choices.label: Ask them to wait
choices.result: You ask them to wait a year, until your contract is settled. They agree, and something goes quiet between you.

scenarios.title: The Weekend Away
scenarios.text: A rare weekend away from the city, at a cabin with no neighbors and one bar of signal. Your phone won't stop buzzing anyway: agents, reporters, a teammate's crisis.

choices.label: Turn the phone off
choices.result: Off, in a drawer, for two days. Nothing burns down, and you come back calmer than you've been since August.

choices.label: Check it once a day
choices.result: Once a day, after dinner, for twenty minutes. You answer what matters and let the rest wait, and it works.

choices.label: Answer the teammate
choices.result: The teammate's crisis gets an hour on the porch, on the phone. You lose an afternoon, and he's grateful for years.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Leadership Award
scenarios.text: The club names you its veteran leadership honoree. The award comes with a dinner, a speech, and a young team that will be listening to every word.

choices.label: Accept and speak
choices.result: You accept and talk to the young players about the year you nearly lost your job. The room is silent, and three rookies find you afterward.

choices.label: Share it
choices.result: You bring the specialists up with you and make them stand there while you thank them. {holder} is mortified and delighted.

choices.label: Accept quietly
choices.result: You accept quietly and thank the equipment staff in a handwritten note. They pin it to the wall of the equipment room.

scenarios.title: The Media Feud
scenarios.text: A columnist has a feud with you, nobody knows why, and every column is about you: your age, your contract, your 'declining leg'. {parent} has started writing letters to the editor.

choices.label: Ignore every column
choices.result: Not one column read, not one word said. He runs out of things to say by December and starts writing about the punter.

choices.label: Invite him to practice
choices.result: An invitation to watch practice, from the sideline, for a whole day. The next column is kinder, and he admits you're still good.

choices.label: Put the columns on your garage wall
choices.result: Every column, printed and pinned to the garage wall where you kick. It's very motivating, a little strange, and {parent} adds his letters.
